prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves in-flight JSON-response-mode POST requests hanging: cleanup deletes the stream/request mappings without ever resolving the Promise<Response> that handleRequest() is waiting on, so the HTTP request stays open until the platform's own socket timeout fires. Its changeset also states the fix carries through to NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport, which wraps this transport. #2692's version is narrower: it only resolves pending responses (using a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error) and groups outstanding request ids per stream for batched POSTs, reusing an already-set real response instead of overwriting it — a batched-request nuance #2600's description does not mention. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the same close() code path to resolve pending JSON-mode responses instead of leaving them hanging, so they will conflict directly. #2600 covers a superset of the problem: in addition to settling parked JSON-mode POSTs (with a 404 'Session not found' response), it also clears _requestToStreamMapping, which #2692 leaves untouched, and re-checks the request/stream correlation after the storeEvent() await race in send() — a second bug in the same close() path. Its changeset also states the fix carries through to NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport, which wraps this transport. #2692's version is narrower: it only resolves pending responses (using a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error) and groups outstanding request ids per stream for batched POSTs, reusing an already-set real response instead of overwriting it — a batched-request nuance #2600's description does not mention. Picking #2600 keeps the broader fix; #2692's batched-request grouping and error-shape handling should be folded in during review since #2600 doesn't clearly demonstrate it covers that case.

clusters.pick_reason: #2763 ships a changeset (required by this repo's release process; #2817 has none) and its description covers both failure modes end-to-end: the hard cap when no progress notifications arrive (`_setupTimeout` now arms `Math.min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout)`) and re-arming against the remaining budget on progress resets. #2817's one-line change only updates `info.startTime` on each progress reset, which is a narrower fix to the same reset path and, if applied on top of or instead of #2763, would keep pushing the total-timeout reference point forward on every progress notification — undermining the hard-cap guarantee #2763 establishes rather than complementing it.

members.author: claxman
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same timeout-reset code path in packages/core-internal/src/shared/protocol.ts that governs how `maxTotalTimeout` interacts with progress-notification-driven timer resets. #2763's changeset explicitly states its fix includes 'progress resets re-arm against the remaining budget' — the same code region #2817 touches (the block that does `clearTimeout(info.timeoutId); info.timeoutId = setTimeout(...)` on a progress reset). #2817 adds only `info.startTime = Date.now()` at that reset point with no changeset, which resets the reference point used for total-timeout accounting on every progress notification — the opposite of a 'hard cap ... even when progress notifications arrive', which is precisely the bug #2763 is titled to fix. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs edit the same close() code path to resolve pending JSON-mode responses instead of leaving them hanging, so they will conflict directly. #2600 covers a superset of the problem: in addition to settling parked JSON-mode POSTs (with a 404 'Session not found' response), it also clears _requestToStreamMapping, which #2692 leaves untouched, and re-checks the request/stream correlation after the storeEvent() await race in send() — a second bug in the same close() path. Its changeset also states the fix carries through to NodeStreamableHTTPServerTransport, which wraps this transport. #2692's version is narrower: it only resolves pending responses (using a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error) and groups outstanding request ids per stream for batched POSTs, reusing an already-set real response instead of overwriting it — a batched-request nuance #2600's description does not mention. Picking #2600 keeps the broader fix; #2692's batched-request grouping and error-shape handling should be folded in during review since #2600 doesn't clearly demonstrate it covers that case.

clusters.pick_reason: #2763 ships a changeset (required by this repo's release process; #2817 has none) and its description covers both failure modes end-to-end: the hard cap when no progress notifications arrive (`_setupTimeout` now arms `Math.min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout)`) and re-arming against the remaining budget on progress resets. #2817's one-line change only updates `info.startTime` on each progress reset, which is a narrower fix to the same reset path and, if applied on top of or instead of #2763, would keep pushing the total-timeout reference point forward on every progress notification — undermining the hard-cap guarantee #2763 establishes rather than complementing it.

members.author: claxman
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both patch the same timeout-reset code path in packages/core-internal/src/shared/protocol.ts that governs how `maxTotalTimeout` interacts with progress-notification-driven timer resets. #2763's changeset explicitly states its fix includes 'progress resets re-arm against the remaining budget' — the same code region #2817 touches (the block that does `clearTimeout(info.timeoutId); info.timeoutId = setTimeout(...)` on a progress reset). #2817 adds only `info.startTime = Date.now()` at that reset point with no changeset, which resets the reference point used for total-timeout accounting on every progress notification — the opposite of a 'hard cap ... even when progress notifications arrive', which is precisely the bug #2763 is titled to fix.
